messages:
maria: quick sync — noticed our Dedicated-preemptible mix cost went up despite lower qps. suspect our cooldowns + conservative surge budget are keeping too many warm nodes for too long. thinking about a budget-aware backpressure that lets short tails spike p99 slightly but saves infra spend. any objections? :thinking:

josh: can you drop the numbers? how big is 'went up'?
maria: sure, pulled last 7d compare (mixed pool, us-west1 primary).
```
baseline: cost = $11.8k/day, p95=210ms, p99=520ms, interruptions=0.9%
proposal-lite: cost = $10.4k/day (-11.9%), p95=220ms, p99=640ms, interruptions=1.6%
note: savings driven by lowering surge_budget from 18% -> 8% and cooldown 600s -> 180s for spot pools
```
kai: are those interruptions coming from single AZ flaps or widespread preemptions?
anya: mostly us-west1-b spike on 2024-11-02 around 03:20 UTC. autoscaler kept 3 extra nodes online through 10m windows, costing ~0.9k that day. logs: 
```
[2024-11-02T03:18:09Z] nodepool/spot-usw1-b: instance-123 preempted
[2024-11-02T03:18:14Z] autoscaler: attempted replacement -> queued (cooldown)
[2024-11-02T03:19:20Z] autoscaler: scale_up +2 (allocated warm standby from reserve)
[2024-11-02T03:27:12Z] autoscaler: cooldown active, held +2 for 8m 53s
```
maria: right — that hold>warm pattern is expensive. idea: add budget-aware backpressure that does two things: 1) track 1h rolling cost delta per pool, 2) if delta > budget_threshold, reduce surge_budget and shorten warm hold, while enabling short-duration hedges (ephemeral preemptible warm instances that terminate earlier but cheaper).
ops-oncall: main risk is latency-sensitive routes (realtime-webhooks). we should gate this behind per-route overrides and a 10% canary. also need a fast rollback path.
josh: config sketch?
maria: pasted lite policy yaml for discussion:
```
preemptible_policy:
  surge_budget_pct: 8            # target % extra capacity on top of baseline
  reserve_pool_pct: 3           # minimal guaranteed warm reserve
  short_hold_seconds: 180       # how long to keep ephemeral warm instances
  cooldown_seconds: 180         # scale down cooldown for spot pool
  cost_backpressure:
    enabled: true
    window_minutes: 60
    delta_threshold_pct: 6     # if cost rises >6% vs baseline, trigger backpressure
  hedging:
    ephemeral_ratio: 0.25      # allocate a quarter of surge as short-lived hedges
    max_hedge_lifetime_sec: 300
```
kai: can we simulate the impact before rolling? maybe replay 7d autoscaler events with the policy and estimate p99 increase. i can run a quick Monte Carlo on eviction traces.
anya: I ran a small replay overnight on a slice (10% traffic) — results matched the rough numbers above. p99 rose selectively on taily workloads (batch rerank), but web interactive latencies remained within SLO when overrides applied.
ops-oncall: ok add canary + tenant override and a kill-switch flag in console. i'd like alerts when p99 > SLO for 5m during experiment.
autoscaler-bot: experiment scheduled: job=preemptible-budget-canary, cohort=10%, start=2024-11-05T01:00Z, rollback_on=[p99>750ms:5m, error_rate:+2%:10m]
josh: sweet. next steps: document rollout playbook, add per-tenant override, run replay with kai on full-week traces, and schedule canary. i'll own the playbook.
maria: thanks — i'll update infra RFC with the config and expected savings. tagging @ops-oncall for the alert hooks. :thumbsup:
